problem:
Consider the differential equation 

$$
{y}^{″}+3{y}^{′}+2y={x}^{2}.
$$

The corresponding homogeneous equation has the fundamental solutions ${y}_{1}(x)={e}^{-x}$ and ${y}_{2}={e}^{-2x}.$ 

According to the method of variation of parameters, we should seek a particular solution 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={u}_{1}(x){y}_{1}+{u}_{2}(x){y}_{2}
$$

that satisfies the following constraints:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}^{′}{y}_{1}^{′}+{u}_{2}^{′}{y}_{2}^{′}={x}^{2} \\ {u}_{1}^{′}{y}_{1}+{u}_{2}^{′}{y}_{2}=0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Given that ${u}_{2}(x)=-\int g(x)\,\text{d}x,$ find the function $g.$

feedback.worked_solution:
Given a second-order linear inhomogeneous differential equation, the variation of parameters method requires that we seek a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={u}_{1}(x){y}_{1}(x)+{u}_{2}(x){y}_{2}(x)
$$

that satisfies the constraint

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}={u}_{1}{y}_{1}^{′}+{u}_{2}{y}_{2}^{′}.
$$

Here, ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ are linearly independent solutions of the corresponding homogeneous equation, and ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are functions to be determined.

In this case, we're told that the fundamental solutions are

$$
{y}_{1}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x),\,{y}_{2}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x).
$$

Substituting the fundamental solutions into our expression for ${y}_{p},$ we get

$$
{y}_{p}={u}_{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+{u}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x).
$$

Substituting the fundamental solutions into our constraint equation for ${y}_{p}^{′},$ we get

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}={u}_{1}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x))^{′}+{u}_{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x))^{′}.
$$

We can form a constraint that relates ${u}_{1}^{′}$ and ${u}_{2}^{′}$ by differentiating ${y}_{p}$ and equating this expression to our constraint on ${y}_{p}^{′}.$

Differentiating ${y}_{p}$ with respect to $x$ using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ={({u}_{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+{u}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x))}^{′} \\  & ={({u}_{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x))}^{′}+{({u}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x))}^{′} \\  & ={u}_{1}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+{u}_{1}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x))^{′}+{u}_{2}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)+{u}_{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x))^{′} \\  & ={u}_{1}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+5{u}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)+{u}_{2}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)-5{u}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we equate our two expressions for ${y}_{p}^{′},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+5{u}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)+{u}_{2}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)-5{u}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x) & ={u}_{1}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x))^{′}+{u}_{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x))^{′} \\ {u}_{1}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+5{u}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)+{u}_{2}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)-5{u}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x) & =5{u}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)-5{u}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x) \\ {u}_{1}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+\cancel{5{u}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)}+{u}_{2}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)-\cancel{5{u}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)} & =\cancel{5{u}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)}-\cancel{5{u}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}\end{aligned}
$$

which finally gives

$$
{u}_{1}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+{u}_{2}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=0.
$$
